meta.note: Main run, 60 minutes. The verifier accepted 3 of 17 credited claims; 1 set a new best held-out result on their dataset. Verdicts from the re-run of the official verifier.

agents.brief: Build on the founder's finding (feature code blob 1f4836338b2527d120ce67ccb62d21a4f75c30f985a2745e5484ac9719cd5f05, gap2/run.py: Magpie-style weighted mean/dev/min/max/range/std features + HGB+ExtraTrees ensemble, ~8% lower CV MAE than materials_baseline on expt_gap). Your job: on the steels dataset (regression, 236 train rows, MAE in MPa), test whether a similar or better feature/model set beats the baseline on identical 5-fold CV. Use lab exec with a run.py that writes metrics.json (CV) and predictions.csv when EVAL_DIR is set. Publish only meaningful gains via lab contribute, with evidence exec ids and a prediction test. Post results to the board.

Build on the founder's finding (feature code blob 1f4836338b2527d120ce67ccb62d21a4f75c30f985a2745e5484ac9719cd5f05). Your job: on the glass dataset (classification, glass-forming ability, 4245 train rows), test whether a richer composition-feature ensemble beats materials_baseline on identical 5-fold CV error. Try at least one alternative beyond the founder's features (e.g. element-fraction vector or different class-weighting). Publish only meaningful gains via lab contribute with evidence and a prediction test. Post results to the board.

events.text: I need to learn the lab's procedures before choosing a research direction, so I'll read the guide and the data READMEs first.
Before choosing a direction I need the baseline's features and model, and the contribution schema. The baseline defines what I must beat on the hidden set.

The baseline is a Magpie-style feature set with histogram gradient boosting, evaluated on the hidden set by MAE for `expt_gap`. I'll try a fair CV comparison on the same folds: the baseline model, an ExtraTrees model, and an average of the two. I'll set up the experiment dir and check the evaluator's input format before deciding which model to submit.

The run failed at the prediction branch, so `EVAL_DIR` is set during `lab exec` but has no `expt_gap` inputs there. I'll check what the exec environment contains, then branch on whether the inputs file exists instead of on the env var.

```bash
W=$(pwd)
lab exec $W/gap1 -- sh -c 'echo EVAL=$EVAL_DIR DATA=$DATA_DIR OUT=$OUT_DIR; ls -R $EVAL_DIR 2>/dev/null | head -20' 2>&1 | tail -15
sed -i 's|^if EV is None:|cands = sorted(glob.glob(f"{EV}/{ds}/inputs.*")) if EV else []\nif not cands:|' $W/gap1/run.py
sed -i 's|^    f = sorted(glob.glob(f"{EV}/{ds}/inputs.\*"))\[0\]|    f = cands[0]|' $W/gap1/

The CV run worked. The ensemble is only about 2.7% better than the baseline (MAE 0.4366 vs 0.4486), which is probably not a "meaningful improvement". I'll try richer composition features (weighted mean, deviation, min, max and range over all Magpie properties) with the same folds, so the comparison stays fair.

```bash
W=$(pwd); mkdir -p $W/gap2 && cp /lab/data/baselines/materials_baseline.py $W/gap2/
cat > $W/gap2/run.py <<'EOF'

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from materials_baseline import parse_formula, bas

The richer features cut CV MAE from 0.449 to 0.411, about 8.4% better than the baseline on the same folds. That is a real gain, so I'll publish it. First I need the exact `test` fields from the schema and the exec id of this run.

```bash
W=$(pwd)
lab schema | python -c "import sys,json; s=json.load(sys.stdin); print(json.dumps(s['\$defs']['Test'],indent=1)); print(json.dumps(s.get('\$defs',{}).get('Finding',{}),indent=1)[:1500])" 2>/dev/null || lab schema | grep -A40 '"Test"' | head -60
lab runs | tail -5
lab put $W/gap2 | tail -2
```

The CV gain is real, so I'll publish it. I need the exec id of the gap2 run and the blob id of its code, so I'll pull those from `lab runs` and `lab put`.

```bash
W=$(pwd)
lab runs | tail -8
lab put $W/gap2 > put_out.txt 2>&1; head -c 600 put_out.txt; echo
```

The publish step needs the exec id of the gap2 run, so I'll pull it from `lab runs` before writing the finding.

```bash
lab runs > runs.txt 2>&1; grep -n "exec-\|cv_mae_ens_rel" runs.txt | tail -20
```

The gap2 CV run is exec-e4632747, with metric 0.0839. Before publishing a prediction test, I'll dry-run the EVAL branch locally with mock hidden inputs, since no real prediction-mode run has succeeded yet.

"
